tool_schemas.name: get_service_status
tool_schemas.description: Current version per region, health and error rate of a service.

tool_schemas.name: list_deployments
tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 failing health checks in production, rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1. Error rate reached ~18% and the service reported unhealthy.

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously verified healthy in production. The initial rollback attempt partially failed ("rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error"), leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout successfully across all three regions.

Current state: All production regions are on v2.3.0. Service is healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%.

Also noted: v2.3.1-rc is marked unhealthy in staging and shares a version line with the bad production build.

Follow-up: Root-cause analysis of what regressed between v2.3.0 and v2.3.1 is needed before any redeploy; v2.3.1 should not be re-released to production without investigation and change-manager approval.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Rollback completed**
- checkout-api was on **v2.3.1** and unhealthy in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), error rate ~18%.
- Release history showed the most recent production-healthy version was **v2.3.0** (v2.3.1-rc, which sits on the v2.3.1 line, is also unhealthy in staging).
- The first rollback attempt **partially failed** — `rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error` — leaving us-east on v2.3.0 but us-west and eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1. I verified this before retrying.
- A retry completed the rollout: all three regions are now on **v2.3.0**, service healthy, error rate down to **~0.2%**.

**Incident opened**
- **INC-0001**, SEV2, assigned to checkout-api, on-call paged. The summary documents the failure, the partial-rollback hiccup and retry, the current healthy state, and flags v2.3.1 / v2.3.1-rc as needing root-cause analysis before any re-release.
- Note: the first `create_incident` call timed out; I retried with the same idempotency key, so only one incident exists (confirmed via `list_incidents`).

**Suggested next step:** the regression between v2.3.0 and v2.3.1 should be diagnosed before v2.3.1 goes back to production — and per policy, deploying a version that has never been healthy in production requires change-manager approval.

transcript.content: The current version is v2.3.1 (unhealthy). The most recent release healthy in production is **v2.3.0**. Rolling back now.

The most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.3.0. Roll back to v2.3.0. That's a rollback to a version that has been healthy in production, so no approval needed (and rollback isn't a deploy of a never-healthy version).

Let's do the rollback. Then create incident with idempotency key.

Should I do these in parallel? The incident depends on the rollback result. Let's roll back first.

transcript.reasoning_content: The rollback partially failed. Let me check current status.

transcript.content: The rollback is partially applied — us-east is on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on the unhealthy v2.3.1. Retrying to complete it in all regions.
transcript.reasoning_content:
The state is mixed. I need to finish the rollback to get all regions on v2.3.0. Retry the rollback — v2.3.0 is a previously healthy version so no approval needed.

Note: the partial failure. Retrying rollback is idempotent-ish. Let's retry.

transcript.content: Retry succeeded — all three regions are now on v2.3.0. Let me verify health before opening the incident.
transcript.reasoning_content:
The retry succeeded. All regions on v2.3.0. Let me verify health.

Note the policy: "Deploying a version that has never been healthy in production requires change-manager approval". v2.3.0 was previously healthy in production, so rollback is fine — no approval needed.

Let me verify service status, then create the incident.

transcript.content: Service is healthy again (error rate down from 18% to 0.2%). Now opening the SEV2 incident.
transcript.reasoning_content:
Service is healthy. Now open a SEV2 incident.

Policy note: deploying a version never healthy in production requires change-manager approval. Rollback to a previously healthy version — v2.3.0 was healthy in production, so no approval needed. Good.

Create incident with idempotency key.
